name: consistency-violation-second-root
description: A `create` of a second composition declaring `root: true`. Every field is admissible — the payload is exactly what `discover` declares for the kind — and every reference resolves (the composition names no member and no delegation); what the assembled staged result breaks is `check-model`'s cardinality over the whole `compositions/` layer, `composition.multiple-roots`: exactly one composition is the top of the emitted hierarchy. The case the tenth code, `consistency-violation`, exists for.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model, whose `compositions/` layer declares exactly one root, `Root`. The change set adds `Root2` beside it with `root: true`, a `title` (a required field) and nothing else.

authorization.notes: The scope covers the create exactly, so the refusal is the model rule and not the authorization boundary.

context.notes: The payload carries the required `title` and no members, so the ONLY thing wrong with the staged result is the second root: `check-model` over the staged result reports `composition.multiple-roots` and nothing else (probed on a copy of `examples/basic` on 2026-10-16, before this vector was recorded from the live engine). A member naming an undeclared component, or a missing `title`, would be answered one pass earlier and the vector would not isolate the code it exists to pin.

expected.notes: BOTH compositions are named, and neither is called the offender: the rule is that exactly one declares `root: true`, and choosing which of the two keeps it is a decision the rule does not make and the model cannot make for the architect — the same shape as `negative/consistency-violation-second-processor.json`, where the layer holds one processor. A client repairs this by removing either address, or by clearing one `root` flag, in a change set of its own. This is NOT `broken-reference`: nothing dangles. Nor is it `schema-violation`: the payload is exactly what `discover` declares, and no single-document check can see the rule, because "exactly one file declares the root" is a statement about every file at once.
